name: Ajaccio

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Sangiovese, Grenache, Sauvignon Blanc, Sémillon and Cabernet Franc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Sangiovese and Grenache sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay.
soil.top: The topsoil drains well and still stores water for dry spells, so vines grow evenly. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 7°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Much of it is steep. Cold air and rain run off, so frost and waterlogging are rare and soils stay thin, keeping yields low. Steep rows are slow and costly to work, often by hand.

winkler: Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
